**Finding submitted: deviation (IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data), confidence 0.85.**

What I found in Section 7 (Materials), which sits inside the mis-numbered §5.4 block:

- **Default ownership runs to IBM.** §7(a) makes Type II the default, and §7(c) defines Type II to include Materials "created during the Service performance period" — so deliverables we pay for default to IBM ownership.
- **Licence back is too narrow.** Our Type II licence is use/reproduce/display/distribute "within Customer's Enterprise only" — no modification, no derivative works, no contractor or sublicence rights, and "Enterprise" is capped at US entities.
- **Our own work product is licensed out broadly.** §7(b) requires us to grant IBM an irrevocable, worldwide licence to distribute Type I Materials externally and to authorise others to do the same — exploitation beyond performing the Services.
- **No Customer Data ownership statement.** §11.6 only allocates responsibility for Content, and §14.17 grants nothing beyond express licences, so there is no affirmation that we retain rights in Content/Customer Components.

Redline (validated ok:true): flip the default to Type I; confine Type II to IBM's pre-existing/generic tools and know-how with a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free, sublicensable licence covering IBM IP embedded in deliverables; limit IBM's licence in our Type I Materials to performing the Services; and add a new §7(e) confirming we retain all rights in Content, Customer Components and data, with no assignment to IBM and no joint ownership. The comment flags the fallback (IBM keeps generic tools/know-how) if IBM will not move the default.
